settingText: PRESENT — modern Neo-Vectra transit plaza during morning rush, ordinary commuters suddenly reacting to memories that do not belong to their present biographies.
summary: Public memory return reaches Neo-Vectra. Strangers recognize old names, dead relatives, former loyalties and injuries that current history says never existed. Theo, Rae and Adrian arrive as a crowd begins turning private contradiction into public panic.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Morning rush in Neo-Vectra. Commuters, bags, coffee, transit noise. One woman stops dead when she sees a man she does not know. Keep the event small inside an ordinary crowd.
Panel 2 — Woman: 'I know you.' Man: 'We've never met.' Their bodies disagree with their words: she is frightened by recognition; he is frightened by her certainty.
Panel 3 — Woman: 'You left me at the south gate.' Man: 'What south gate?' Let nearby strangers begin noticing, but do not turn the plaza into riot spectacle.
Panel 4 — Theo, Rae and Adrian enter the edge of the scene. Rae reaches the woman first and says, 'Don't tell her she's wrong.'
Panel 5 — Theo turns from the distressed woman toward Rae: 'What do we tell her?' Rae keeps one hand lightly on the
Panel 6 — woman's forearm and answers, 'That she's here now.' The stranger she remembers remains several feet away, unsure whether to approach.

Panel 7 — End on the woman still looking at the stranger with grief for a relationship neither present biography can explain. The public crisis begins as two people unable to reconcile what they feel.

dialogueInline.text: You left me at the south gate.

settingText: PAST — ancient Neo-Vectra command balcony overlooking a populated city already preparing for war.
summary: Oryon debuts by telling Arbiter that every future in which they wait ends with Neo-Vectra becoming the doorway to a wider catastrophe. Arbiter asks whether Oryon has seen any future in which fear does not become permission.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Ancient Neo-Vectra command balcony above a populated city already preparing for war. Oryon stands at the rail with his gaze fixed on specific families and evacuation crews below; Arbiter watches Oryon's face instead of the tactical display.

Panel 2 — Oryon: 'If we wait, this city becomes the beginning.' Arbiter: 'Of what?' Oryon's shoulders are rigid, both hands locked around the rail and his eyes remain on the people below. Oryon: 'Everything we have been trying to prevent.' Show fear on him before Arbiter challenges the claim.
Panel 3 — Arbiter: 'You've said that before.' Oryon: 'Because it keeps being true.' Arbiter delivers the line without turning from the balcony; Oryon gives a tired sideways glance before answering.
Panel 4 — Arbiter: 'Or because you keep looking for the same ending.' Oryon releases the rail with one hand and turns away from the tactical display, face unsettled and silent.

dialogueInline.text: If we wait, Neo-Vectra is the first city we lose.
The chain reaction we've been trying to stop.
Or because you keep checking until you find it.

Panel 3 — Rae: 'They deserve not to get killed while we're explaining it.' Two strangers in the foreground argue over a recovered

Panel 6 — Rae: 'No. We keep them from choosing a war before they remember why it ended.' End on the symbols held by ordinary people whose present relationships matter as much as the recovered loyalties.

settingText: PAST — ancient Neo-Vectra residential concourse as Atlas shields civilians while Oryon urges evacuation from a city he believes cannot be saved.
summary: Atlas refuses Oryon's demand to abandon Neo-Vectra. Mero sees both arguments: Atlas is saving people in front of him; Oryon believes staying will kill people far beyond the city.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Ancient residential concourse under evacuation. Atlas physically shields civilians while Oryon arrives with Mero urging withdrawal. Surround them with distinct people: a parent with two children, an older medic, a worker carrying a pet carrier and a wounded transit officer.

Panel 2 — Oryon: 'You are saving the people who can see you.' Atlas: 'They're still people.' Atlas remains actively helping someone while answering. Oryon: 'So are the ones who die if this gets out.' His grief points beyond the frame; do not make him cold.

Panel 3 — Atlas: 'Then help me save both.' Oryon: 'There is no both.' Atlas stops moving for one beat; Oryon cannot meet his eyes and looks instead at the civilians passing between them. Mero watches a child or injured civilian pass between the two champions, seeing the cost of turning lives into sides of an argument.
Panel 4 — Mero: 'That false choice keeps ruining us.' Atlas and Oryon stand on opposite sides of the same evacuation lane, each physically helping people move through while neither answers Mero.

dialogueInline.text: You are saving the people who can see you.
So are the ones who die if this gets out.
We don't have enough ships for both.

settingText: PAST — ancient Neo-Vectra command hall with Starbreaker, Redlin and Oryon arguing while Flux's empty place remains conspicuous.
summary: Oryon pushes for pre-emptive action, Starbreaker agrees the danger cannot be allowed to widen, and Redlin sees certainty feeding escalation. Flux's unexplained absence removes the one person who used to challenge all of them from outside the binary.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Ancient command hall. Starbreaker, Redlin, Oryon and Mero occupy a tense table; Flux's familiar place remains conspicuously empty, with an unused chair and abandoned papers/cup motif visible. Compose the page so that empty place remains a recurring visual anchor during the conversation without explaining the absence.
Panel 2 — Oryon: 'We know where this ends.' Redlin: 'No. Flux knew enough to stop saying that.' His eyes move to the empty place.
Panel 3 — Starbreaker: 'Flux left.' Redlin: 'Maybe because none of you listened.' Redlin points once toward Flux's empty chair; Starbreaker looks there instead of back at Redlin.
Panel 4 — Oryon: 'Or because looking became unbearable.' Keep Oryon seated nearest the empty place, eyes on the abandoned cup or papers, shoulders lowered before he looks back to the others.
Panel 5 — Mero: 'Either way, Flux isn't here to choose for us.' End with the empty place still unresolved. Responsibility remains in the room while certainty has left it.

settingText: PRESENT — Neo-Vectra overlook before dawn as contradictory memories continue spreading through the city.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Overlook before dawn. Below, ordinary people continue arguing, reuniting, writing down memories and trying to sleep. Adrian joins Theo and Rae. Adrian: 'You keep asking what happens if everyone remembers.' Theo answers, 'Yes.'
Panel 2 — Adrian gives the first example: someone remembers a wife they never married. Show one ordinary pair below, but do not literalize every example as prophecy.

Panel 3 — Adrian continues: someone remembers killing the man who is now their brother; a city remembers belonging to an enemy that no longer exists. Keep his focus on relationships and identities, not institutions.

Panel 4 — Rae: 'And you thought forgetting was kinder.' Adrian: 'I thought it was the only thing we hadn't tried.' End on Adrian leaning against the overlook rail, shoulders rounded, while below them scattered people write memories, argue quietly and try to sleep under temporary lights.
